1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif face at a comfortable size with roomy line height and clear label/field spacing, though no explicitly dyslexia-tuned font or letter-spacing is evident.

2.why: Every screen uses short sentences in normal sentence case, with no italics, all-caps, or dense paragraphs.

3.why: Content is laid out in a single narrow column with full-width stacked fields and buttons that read well at phone width, although the monospace activity-log panel is less mobile-friendly.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Get a six-digit identity code for this demo.' and 'Next: enter the six digits.' are one line each and in plain wording.

5.why: Placeholders show expected formats ('name@example.com', '123456'), though the password field gives no example.

6.why: No screen contains more than a couple of short lines before the primary action; the longest text is a two-line explanatory note.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control appears anywhere, and the identity code is only shown in the browser console so it must be read and typed manually.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is shown in any of the five screenshots; the authenticator setup step is never reached.

9.why: Standard email/password inputs are present which browsers could autofill, but there is no visible evidence of autocomplete/one-time-code support and the OTP field shows no such affordance.

10.why: A step progress bar, an icon-paired heading, and a single high-contrast filled primary button make the current step and action prominent, though the progress segments are unlabelled.

11.why: Each screen asks for one main action ('Sign in', 'Get identity code', 'Check code'), with only a clearly de-emphasised secondary 'Re-request identity code' button alongside.

12.why: Green confirmation banners plainly state outcome and next step, e.g. 'Signed in successfully. Next: get your identity code.' and 'Your identity code was requested. Next: enter the six digits.'

13.why: The failed code entry can be retried freely and a 'Re-request identity code' button is offered with no lockout or penalty shown, but no reveal/hide toggle for the password or codes is present.

14.why: The error reads 'That code does not match. Check the six digits, or request a new code.' — it names the problem and the remedy without blaming the user.

15.why: An explicit notice states 'There is no reading timer. Take as long as you need.', and no countdown, expiry, or auto-updating element appears on any screen.
